question: For the patients who are diagnosed with SJS, how many of them have a normal level of total protein?
evidence: diagnosed with SJS refers to Diagnosis = 'SJS'; normal level of total protein refers to TP > 6.0 and TP < 8.5;
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Diagnosis = 'SJS' AND T2.TP > 6.0 AND T2.TP < 8.5
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Diagnosis = 'SJS' AND T2.TP > 6.0 AND T2.TP < 8.5

d.request: For the patients diagnosed with SJS (Diagnosis = 'SJS'), how many of them have a normal level of total protein (TP > 6.0 and TP < 8.5), counting each distinct patient ID only once?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P INNER JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.Diagnosis = 'SJS' AND L.TP > 6.0 AND L.TP < 8.5

b.request: Count the distinct patient IDs in Patient with Diagnosis = 'SJS' who have at least one Laboratory record with TP > 6.0 and TP < 8.5, counting each ID only once
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P WHERE P.Diagnosis = 'SJS' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L WHERE L.ID = P.ID AND L.TP > 6.0 AND L.TP < 8.5)

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P INNER JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.Diagnosis = 'SJS' AND L.TP > 6.0 AND L.TP < 8.5
